<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The glow bug stems from a CSS incompatibility between `.text-gradient` and `.glow-text`. These classes use conflicting text-shadow and background-clip properties, which prevents the glow effect from rendering properly.

`text-shadow` fails on transparent text clipped by `background-clip`. `filter: drop-shadow()` is the modern fix. Pseudo-elements and split layers are alternatives.

Drop-shadow follows the rendered alpha channel, so it works correctly with background-clip text. The plan is to add drop-shadow glow directly to `.text-gradient` rather than combining it with `.glow-text`, since text-shadow breaks on transparent gradient text.

A universal drop-shadow fix for `.glow-text` would cover both gradient and plain text without extra classes. The same bug appears in the ContactSection. The tiny 12px cursor dot may be hard to spot even though its bright green color should be visible.

GSAP replaces the cursor's inline `transform` with `translate(x, y)`, which overwrites the existing `translate(-50%, -50%)` centering. This likely misplaces the cursor instead of making it invisible.

Reconsidering the cursor theory: a 12px dot at the exact mouse coordinates should still be visible even if GSAP overwrites the centering transform. The real cause of the nearly invisible cursor remains unclear.

GSAP x/y values are correct for fixed positioning, so the cursor offset is expected and not the cause of invisibility. The follower is a 60% opacity border ring with no fill, while the inner dot is solid. On Windows or high-DPI displays, the 12px size may simply be too small to see clearly.

The cursor shrinks to 6px during hover scaling. The 0.3 follower opacity is just the outer ring, not the dot. A `pointer: fine` media query could hide the cursor on touchscreen laptops. To fix the GSAP transform overwrite, the plan is to combine `xPercent: -50, yPercent: -50` with the x and y coordinates, or use quickSetter to preserve the centering offset.

The cursor will receive a box-shadow glow and a slight size increase to improve visibility. The CSS fix for the glow text bug is now being drafted, replacing text-shadow with filter drop-shadow inside `.glow-text`.</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

You were right — both were real bugs.

**Glow text (`KHODABUX`, “someone who ships?”)**  
Those use `text-gradient` (`bg-clip-text` + `text-transparent`) together with `glow-text` (`text-shadow`). In Chrome/Edge, `text-shadow` gets clipped with gradient text, so some letters glow and others don’t.

**Fix:** For `.text-gradient.glow-text`, use `filter: drop-shadow()` instead — it follows each letter’s shape and glows evenly.

**Custom cursor**  
Two problems:
1. GSAP’s `x`/`y` animation was overwriting `translate(-50%, -50%)`, so the dot wasn’t centered on the pointer.
2. The dot was only 12px and shrank to 6px on hover, while the outer ring faded to 30% opacity — hard to see on a dark background.

**Fix:** Center with GSAP’s `xPercent`/`yPercent`, made the dot slightly larger with a green glow, and on hover it scales up instead of shrinking.

Refresh the page at `http://localhost:8080/` and check the hero name + cursor. If anything still looks off, tell me which browser you’re on.

            "lineNumber": 3,
            "text": "/**"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4,
            "text": " * Observes an element via IntersectionObserver and adds the \"revealed\""
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 5,
            "text": " * class once it enters the viewport. Fires once, then disconnects."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 6,
            "text": " *"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 7,
            "text": " * Attach the returned ref to the element you want to reveal."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 8,
            "text": " * Pair with the &#96;.reveal&#96; / &#96;.reveal-item&#96; CSS classes in index.css."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 9,
            "text": " */"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 10,
            "text": "export function useReveal\u003cT extends HTMLElement = HTMLDivElement\u003e("
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 11,
            "text": "  options?: { threshold?: number; rootMargin?: string }"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 12,
            "text": ") {"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 13,
            "text": "  const ref = useRef\u003cT\u003e(null);"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 15,
            "text": "  useEffect(() =\u003e {"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 16,
            "text": "    const el = ref.current;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 17,
            "text": "    if (!el) return;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 19,
            "text": "    const observer = new IntersectionObserver("
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 20,
            "text": "      ([entry]) =\u003e {"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 21,
            "text": "        if (entry.isIntersecting) {"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 22,
            "text": "          el.classList.add(\"revealed\");"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 23,
            "text": "          observer.unobserve(el);"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 24,
            "text": "        }"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 25,
            "text": "      },"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 26,
            "text": "      {"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27,
            "text": "        threshold: options?.threshold ?? 0.15,"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 28,
            "text": "        rootMargin: options?.rootMargin ?? \"0px\","
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 29,
            "text": "      }"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 30,
            "text": "    );"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 31
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 32,
            "text": "    observer.observe(el);"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 33,
            "text": "    return () =\u003e observer.disconnect();"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 34,
            "text": "  }, []);"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 36,
            "text": "  return ref;"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 37,
            "text": "}"
          }

4. **Stat cards** — removed the `opacity: 0` fade on `.reveal-item` (that was trapping the gradient text in a broken state); they now slide up and the numbers light up instead.

Refresh the page and scroll to the About section — the numbers and "on the first deploy" should pop to bright green on reveal, and KHODABUX should be a solid gradient again with an even glow.

The glow effect is failing because `text-gradient` uses `background-clip: text`, which leaves the element mostly transparent outside the text shape. This prevents the blur layer from properly surrounding the text.

The contact section’s `.reveal` opacity animation may also interfere. Other sections glow correctly because they use solid color with `text-shadow`, avoiding the transparency issue.

The simplest fix is to use solid primary color with `text-shadow` for the visible top layer, keeping the gradient only for the background glow. A pseudo-element blur layer is another option, but SVG is overkill.

The blur layer should use solid primary color instead of `text-gradient`. A duplicate span with `blur-2xl` and `opacity-70` can sit behind the gradient text. Both spans must share identical content and font to align properly. A dedicated CSS class would keep the markup cleaner.

A pseudo-element approach is cleaner. A `::before` layer with solid primary color, `blur(20px)`, and `opacity-0.75` can sit behind the gradient text. The component should accept a `data-text` attribute to duplicate the exact text string for alignment.

The pseudo-element blur layer must inherit the parent font and size to align perfectly with the gradient text. It should use solid primary color with no background-clip, letting the blur create the glow.

The hero section’s `overflow-hidden` is clipping the blur glow. Removing it or moving overflow to the ThreeScene container will let the glow extend past the text bounds. The contact section likely has no such overflow rule, so its blur layer may still fail despite the solid-color approach.

The `::before` pseudo-element will use `attr(data-text)` to duplicate the exact text string for perfect alignment. The hero section should switch to `overflow-x-hidden` or `overflow-visible` on the name wrapper rather than removing `overflow-hidden` entirely. A stronger glow can be achieved with `blur-xl`, higher opacity, and multiple layered `text-shadow` effects on a solid underlay.

The pseudo-element will use `blur(20px) brightness(1.2)` with `opacity-0.85` and `white-space: nowrap` to prevent wrapping. An outer glow layer via `::after` is being added for a larger surrounding blur.

The outer glow layer will use `blur(40px)` at `opacity-0.5` for a softer surrounding glow. The hero section’s `overflow-hidden` may not be the real culprit, since the large centered text keeps the blur mostly inside the viewport. The blur is more likely being clipped by the text span’s own containing block.

The hero section’s `overflow-hidden` is confirmed to clip the blur glow. The fix is to remove `overflow-hidden` from the hero and move it onto a dedicated wrapper around `ThreeScene`, since the particles are absolutely positioned and can safely be clipped there.</details></think>

import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import gsap from "gsap";

const CustomCursor = () =&gt; {
  const cursorRef = useRef&lt;HTMLDivElement&gt;(null);
  const followerRef = useRef&lt;HTMLDivElement&gt;(null);
  const [isPointerFine, setIsPointerFine] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() =&gt; {
    const mq = window.matchMedia("(pointer: fine)");
    const set = () =&gt; setIsPointerFine(mq.matches);
    set();
    mq.addEventListener("change", set);
    return () =&gt; mq.removeEventListener("change", set);
  }, []);

  useEffect(() =&gt; {
    if (!isPointerFine) return;
    const cursor = cursorRef.current;
    const follower = followerRef.current;
    if (!cursor || !follower) return;

    const moveCursor = (e: MouseEvent) =&gt; {
      gsap.to(cursor, { x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY, duration: 0.1, ease: "power2.out" });
      gsap.to(follower, { x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY, duration: 0.4, ease: "power2.out" });
    };

    const handleMouseEnter = () =&gt; {
      gsap.to(follower, { scale: 2.5, opacity: 0.3, duration: 0.3 });
      gsap.to(cursor, { scale: 0.5, duration: 0.3 });
    };

    const handleMouseLeave = () =&gt; {
      gsap.to(follower, { scale: 1, opacity: 0.6, duration: 0.3 });
      gsap.to(cursor, { scale: 1, duration: 0.3 });
    };

    window.addEventListener("mousemove", moveCursor);

    const interactiveElements = document.querySelectorAll("a, button, [data-cursor-hover]");
    interactiveElements.forEach((el) =&gt; {
      el.addEventListener("mouseenter", handleMouseEnter);
      el.addEventListener("mouseleave", handleMouseLeave);
    });

    return () =&gt; {
      window.removeEventListener("mousemove", moveCursor);
      interactiveElements.forEach((el) =&gt; {
        el.removeEventListener("mouseenter", handleMouseEnter);
        el.removeEventListener("mouseleave", handleMouseLeave);
      });
    };
  }, [isPointerFine]);

  if (!isPointerFine) return null;

  return (
    &lt;&gt;
      &lt;div
        ref={cursorRef}

**What was actually wrong**
GSAP was animating `opacity` on elements that use `text-gradient` + `glow-text`. That breaks gradient text and its glow in the browser — it looked dark, patchy, or over-blown depending on the workaround.

**What changed**
- Removed `GradientGlowText`, `text-accent`, pseudo-element glows, and related CSS
- Restored original `text-gradient` + `glow-text` on **KHODABUX** and **someone who ships?**
- **Hero:** KHODABUX only slides up now — no opacity fade (gradient stays intact)
- **Contact:** ScrollTrigger slide-in without fading the gradient line
- **About:** new `useScrollGlow` hook — GSAP ScrollTrigger animates color + glow from dim green → bright on scroll (stats + “on the first deploy”)

Refresh and check those three spots. The about section should animate in on scroll; the hero and footer should show normal gradient text with a subtle glow, not a heavy halo.
